subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining repair target the scheduled producer that asks for invalid paths, or should OpenClaw change the generic read tool contract to treat directory reads as listings?
rationale: Current source still supports a directory-read failure shape, but changing read-tool semantics is broader than the reported scheduler/RSS symptom and could affect model-facing tool behavior.

options.title: Reproduce and fix producer path
options.body: Collect current gateway/cron RSS proof, then fix the scheduled prompt or producer that requests memory-system/CORE.md or agent-tasks as a file.

options.title: Change read-directory semantics
options.body: Make the read tool return a directory listing for directory paths, accepting a broader model-facing tool contract change.

options.title: Wait for reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but require fresh redacted logs and current-version memory diagnostics before choosing the implementation boundary.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and fix producer path
recommendation.body: Collect current gateway/cron RSS proof, then fix the scheduled prompt or producer that requests memory-system/CORE.md or agent-tasks as a file.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent read-tool and heartbeat work makes this the best available routing owner for the producer-versus-tool-contract decision.
